get_api_info.title: Get API information
get_api_info.description: The API's own version and build, plus the whitelabel and user context the token resolves to. The cheapest call there is, so it doubles as a credential check when you only want to know that the token is live.

output.description: Server version and the context the token belongs to.

whitelabel.description: The whitelabel instance serving this token, when there is one.

user.description: The user the token belongs to.

get_current_user.title: Get the authenticated user
get_current_user.description: Who the token belongs to -- the user's id and username -- alongside the backend and API versions. Use it to resolve the account before creating banners, and prefer it over `get_api_info` when you specifically want the user rather than the deployment.

output.description: The authenticated user and the API version serving them.

create_banner.title: Create a banner
create_banner.description: Render creative from a template. `template_id` picks the template, `modes` says which formats to export (`{"png": true, "video": {"fps": 15, "crf": 28}}`), and `overrides` swaps the template's own copy and images for this creative's, keyed by the item name shown in the editor's sidebar. Rendering is asynchronous: this returns the banner with `status: "exporting"` and no files, so poll `get_banner` with the returned id until `status` is `ready` and read the download links off `files[].url`.

template_id.description: The template to render from, copied from the editor's sidebar.

modes.description: Which formats to export, as a map of mode to options -- `html5` (`packed`, `flexible`), `png`, `jpeg`, `webp`, `pdf` and `amp` take `true`; `video` takes `fps` and `crf` (lower is better quality) and an optional `audio` object; `gif` takes `fps` and `frames`. One file comes back per mode.

html5.description: Animated HTML5, optionally packed into one file.

gif.description: Animated GIF; takes fps and frames.

video.description: Video; takes fps, crf and audio.

overrides.description: What to change about the template, keyed by item name -- each value takes `text` for copy, `url` for an external image, `references` for an image already uploaded to the library, and `css` for style rules such as `{"color": "red"}`. Omit it and the banner renders the template's own content unchanged.

size_ids.description: Which of the template's sizes to export. Pass the size ids, or the single string `all` for every size the template defines.

sizes.description: Per-size override objects, for creative whose copy differs between formats. Use `size_ids` instead when every size shares the same content.

clicktag.description: The click-through URL to bake into the creative's clicktag.

template_data.description: A serialised AdRapid player document, for rendering creative that was composed outside a stored template. Mutually exclusive with the template's own content.

output.description: The new banner, still exporting -- poll `get_banner` for its files.

id.description: The banner id to poll with.

get_banner.title: Get a banner
get_banner.description: One banner by id, with its render `status` and, once that reads `ready`, the `files` array holding a `url` per exported format. This is the poll half of `create_banner`; a render that could not finish comes back `failed` with the reason in `failedReason`.

banner_id.description: The banner's id, as returned by `create_banner`.

output.description: The banner, with its files once the render is ready.

files.description: One entry per exported format, each with name, type, width, height and url.

failedReason.description: Why the render failed, when it did.

templateId.description: An immutable template holding this banner's content, cloneable into a new banner.

list_banners.title: List banners
list_banners.description: The account's banners, newest first, with their render status. Narrow with `search` over the name and with `status` to pick out the ones still exporting or the ones that failed. Returns a `count` and a `rows` array; page with `offset` and `limit`.

search.description: Filter banners whose name matches this string.

status.description: Only banners in this render state.

limit.description: How many banners to return. AdRapid's own floor is 10.

offset.description: How many banners to skip, for paging.

output.description: A page of banners and the total matching the filter.

count.description: How many banners match in total.

list_templates.title: List templates
list_templates.description: The templates available to the account -- the starting point for every banner, since `create_banner` needs a `templateId`. Narrow with `search` over the template name. Returns a `count` and a `rows` array.

search.description: Filter templates whose name matches this string.

limit.description: How many templates to return. AdRapid's own floor is 10.

offset.description: How many templates to skip, for paging.

output.description: A page of templates and the total matching the filter.

count.description: How many templates match in total.

rows.description: Each with id, name, ownerId and the template data.

list_media.title: List media
list_media.description: Images and video already uploaded to the account's library, with their mime type and transcoding status. These are the assets an `overrides` entry can point at by reference rather than by external url.

search.description: Filter media whose name matches this string.

limit.description: How many media items to return. AdRapid's own floor is 10.

offset.description: How many media items to skip, for paging.

output.description: A page of media items and the total matching the filter.

count.description: How many media items match in total.

rows.description: Each with id, name, mimeType, status and progress.

list_fonts.title: List fonts
list_fonts.description: The fonts the account can render with -- Google, Adobe and custom uploads alike -- with the family name, the weights and styles available as `variants`, and the character `subsets` each covers. Useful before overriding a text item's `css` with a `font-family` the account may not have.

search.description: Filter fonts whose name matches this string.

limit.description: How many fonts to return. AdRapid's own floor is 10.

offset.description: How many fonts to skip, for paging.

output.description: A page of fonts and the total matching the filter.

count.description: How many fonts match in total.

rows.description: Each with id, family, source, category, variants and subsets.
